cards.title: Chloromethane Polarity And sp3 Geometry
cards.front: In chloromethane, which atom carries δ−, which atom carries δ+, and why is the molecule polar?
cards.back: Chlorine is more electronegative than carbon, so Cl is δ− and the carbon bonded to Cl is δ+. The C-Cl bond dipole is not canceled by the C-H bonds, so chloromethane has a net molecular dipole toward chlorine.

facts: Electronegativity increases from left to right across a row and generally decreases down a group.
A bond dipole points toward the more electronegative atom.
Partial negative charge, δ−, appears on the more electronegative end of a polar bond.
Carbon is less electronegative than chlorine, so the C-Cl bond is polarized Cδ+-Clδ−.
The C-Cl sigma bond can be pictured as overlap between a carbon sp3 orbital and a chlorine valence orbital along the internuclear axis.
A molecule can contain polar bonds but have no net dipole if the bond dipoles cancel by symmetry.

prompts.question: Which atom is more electronegative in C-Cl?
Assign δ+ and δ− for the C-Cl bond.
prompts.answer: C is δ+ and Cl is δ−.
